recentItems.title: “Republicans will LOSE the Presidency in 2028” - Anthony Scaramucci
recentItems.description:
Anthony Scaramucci is a Wall Street banker, podcaster and former White House communications director who spent just 11 days working for Donald Trump before being fired. Once a Trump supporter, he has since become one of his most vocal critics, and it would seem that the feeling is mutual, with Trump calling him an "unstable 'nut job'" who showed "gross incompetence" during his 11-day tenure. His new book, All the Wrong Moves, looks at the political and economic decisions he believes helped create the anger and populism that transformed American politics.

In this episode of Ways to Change the World, Scaramucci talks to Krishnan Guru-Murthy about his time inside the Trump White House, why he believes America’s political system needs reform, the role of big money in politics, the impact of China, the wars in Afghanistan and Iraq and the 2008 financial crisis. He also reflects on his Republican identity, why he believes Donald Trump was able to tap into economic and cultural anger, whether the Republican Party can survive Trump, and whether America can find its way back from the political divisions of the last decade.

recentItems.title: ‘I was fighting for my life’ - Flydubai pilot talks to Indian PM
recentItems.description:
Indian pilot Smit Machchhar has been hailed a hero for opening the cockpit door of the Israel-bound Flydubai flight, after being stabbed by his fellow pilot.

[Subscribe to our Substack newsletter: https://channel4news.substack.com/subscribe]

The plane, travelling from Dubai to Tel Aviv, had over 170 people on board when Mr Machchhar was attacked and the plane plummeted more than 17,000ft.

By opening the door, passengers and crew were able to overpower the attacker and land the plane safely.

In a video call with Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Captain Machchhar described the moment, while he was “fighting for his life”.

Mr Modi praised the pilot and told him “the whole country is praying for you”.

recentItems.title: The Houthis - Iran’s secret weapon in the Middle East
recentItems.description:
The Houthis have made rapid advances in Yemen, sparking a dormant civil war back to life in the Middle East, threatening their neighbour Saudi Arabia, increasing pressure on international oil supply, in a region already reeling from the US and Israel’s war with Iran. But who are they?

[Subscribe to our Substack newsletter: https://channel4news.substack.com/subscribe]

Once a small Shiite militia from Yemen's northern hills, the Houthis have grown into a fearsome fighting force, utilising modern military technology and growing their numbers allowing them to take swathes of territory along the Red Sea coast, including the Bab al-Mandeb Strait. That has implications for the whole world, making the militia a global threat - the importance of this crucial international shipping lane to the global economy has only grown amid the chaos seen in the Strait of Hormuz.

The Houthis have shown remarkable speed and force to take territory from the Saudi-backed Yemeni government, widely recognised as the legitimate ruler of Yemen by the international community. For Iran, which has long-supplied the Houthis with financial and military backing, these Houthi successes are aiding their cause against the US and Israel. 

But who exactly are this fundamentalist Shiite Islamist group? Why are they so opposed to Saudi Arabia, the US and Israel? How did they rise to power to control the lives of most of Yemen’s population, while Iran's proxy fighting forces, like Hamas and Hezbollah, have been severely weakened in recent years? And what is life actually like for the roughly 30  million Yemenis living under the control of a group the US has designated a terrorist organisation?

We look at all of that in this FourSight and what the latest Houthi successes mean for the Middle East and the rest of the world.

With thanks to Dr Elisabeth Kendall, Afrah Nasser, and Professor Vali Nasr.

recentItems.title: Is the UK prepared for early release of hundreds of prisoners?
recentItems.description:
Outside prisons across England and Wales, hundreds of prisoners walked free as part of the government’s early release scheme. The government said it was essential to ease overcrowding to avoid the justice system collapsing.

[Subscribe to our Substack newsletter: https://channel4news.substack.com/subscribe]

But the sight of prisoners leaving jail early, some thanking Prime Minister Andy Burnham personally, has enraged victims and their families. 

Probation officers have warned they may not have the resources to monitor all of them, while survivors of domestic abuse and violent crimes are fearful at the prospect of offenders being let back into the community.  

The government defends the move as a necessary evil to tackle the crisis in prisons, but victims accuse him of making them pay the price. A price some fear they could pay with their life.

recentItems.title: How did Christa Pike survive two lethal injections?
recentItems.description:
Christa Pike survived two lethal doses of the drug meant to kill her in the state of Tennessee, thirty years after she was convicted of murder. What happens now?   

Now, the Tennessee Governor has ordered a review of the state's capital punishment process.

[Subscribe to our Substack newsletter: https://channel4news.substack.com/subscribe]

Lawyers Christa Pike said she was alive in a critical condition and was receiving life saving medical care. 

It was the second failed execution in Tennessee this year. 

Prison officials involved with Pike's case insisted they had followed "every step" of the state's protocol.

recentItems.title: FlyDubai plane CHAOS: Did Israel nearly face its own ‘9/11’? | The Fourcast Indicators
recentItems.description:
An Israel-bound Flydubai flight plunged more than 14,000 feet in just 30 seconds after the co-pilot allegedly attacked the pilot and tried to take control of the aircraft.

[Subscribe to our Substack newsletter: https://channel4news.substack.com/subscribe]

The plane eventually landed safely in Saudi Arabia after passengers and off-duty pilots intervened, but the incident has raised urgent questions about aviation security, insider threats and whether flights to Israel now face a new kind of risk.

Matt Frei and Mark Urban examine what we know so far, why Benjamin Netanyahu has compared the incident to a potential “9/11-style” attack, and what it could mean for Israel, Flydubai and airline security around the world.

There is currently no evidence linking the alleged attack to Iran or a wider terrorist plot.

recentItems.title: Tennessee Governor suspends all executions after Christa Pike survived lethal injection
recentItems.description:
The Governor of Tennessee has ordered all state executions to be suspended and launched an independent review after an inmate survived attempts to execute her.

[Subscribe to our Substack newsletter: https://channel4news.substack.com/subscribe]

Christa Pike's execution was halted and she was taken to hospital when she was still showing signs of life after receiving two lethal injections.

Governor Bill Lee said he was "highly disappointed".

50-year-old  Pike was sentenced to death in 1996 aged 18 for murdering her 19-year-old schoolmate Colleen Slemmer.

Including Pike, there are 40 people currently on death row in the state of Tennessee.

It is the second failed attempt to execute someone in the U.S. state this year, after prison officials failed to find a suitable vein for the lethal injection of inmate Tony Carruthers, who was also convicted of murder.
